title: Japan As We Saw It
summary: An account of eight weeks in Japan in the autumn of 1891 by M. Bickersteth, who travelled with her father, Edward Henry Bickersteth, Bishop of Exeter, and his party to visit her brother Edward, the English bishop in Japan; the Bishop of Exeter wrote the preface. They cross Canada by rail to Vancouver and sail to Yokohama, then see Tokyo and its Anglican missions, Nikko and Ikao, Miyanoshita and Hakone, Nagoya, Kyoto, Osaka, and Nara. A long chapter gives newspaper reports of the great earthquake of 28 October 1891, which the party lived through at Osaka, and letters from the stricken towns of Gifu and Ogaki. The journey goes on by Fukuyama, Kobe, and the Inland Sea to Kyushu (Fukuoka, Kumamoto and the volcano of Aso, Nagasaki), and home by Hong Kong, Canton, Singapore, and Colombo. Notes at the end list the Anglican clergy and missions in Japan.
